chunks.text: When Albert Einstein was 16 years old, he imagined himself riding alongside a beam of light.
He used this picture in mind to help him when working out the theory of relativity.
Daydreaming, called Thought Experiments by Einstein, can make you have wild imaginings.
We can imagine different landscapes, like mountains and forests.
It lets your mind walk slowly around things that aren't happening right now.
It means thinking ahead to a holiday or a birthday party.
Disappearing into a daydream lets your mind escape when things are difficult.
It helps you deal with worries and fears.
For example, imagining how you're going to speak up in class is like practising the scene in your head,
which can make you feel calmer.
Imagining graduating encourages you to work harder towards your learning goals.
Reading literature also inspires our creativity in daydreaming.
When we picture ourselves as a princess or a queen wearing a beautiful dress,
we let our minds wander in a fairy tale that brings us courage.
Then we may pick up our pens to write our own paragraphs.
However, try not to let your mind be absent when you need to focus in class or cross the road.
Instead, find a time when you don't have to focus on anything,
like going for a walk or brushing your teeth.
Research shows that people often come up with more solutions to problems after daydreaming because it is similar to staying at a hotel,
where we can take a break.
So next time you're stuck on homework, stop for a moment and see where your daydreams take you.
